purpose: W6-A: establish provider-neutral bank capabilities and receipt/finality boundaries over the canonical SettlementPlan/bank-operation authority, with Sber as the primary reference mapping and Alfa-Bank/T-Bank as additional conformance targets, without claiming live credentials or creating bank-specific core semantics.
authorization: Owner instruction on 2026-09-21 to continue bank/finance product and integration work without a second settlement core, combined with the earlier staged W6-A scope. Implementation authority still requires this governance scope to pass review and merge on current main.

dependencies.canonicalBankSettlementReadContract: PRODUCT-MULTIBANK-CANONICAL-READ-CONTRACT-20260921; required before any PRODUCT screen binds a concrete Deal/bank operation to a provider/binding/finality state

sourceAuditFindings: The exact-main gap map says bank-neutral settlement, holds, callback keys and pending bank operations already exist, but outbound bank consumers, a complete adapter, BillingPort, FinancingPort, bank binding and live finality receipts are absent. This scope must extend those authorities rather than create a second money engine.

config/integration/integration.env.example currently contains BANK_MODE=sandbox, BANK_PROVIDER=sber and BANK_CALLBACK_VERIFY=false. Those example values are configuration examples only and are forbidden as readiness, callback-verification or production-success evidence.

apps/web/lib/platform-v7/integrations/providerRegistry.ts exposes Sber-labelled provider codes for presentation/routing. UI provider metadata is not bank authority and cannot choose a tenant bank binding or advance Settlement.

apps/web/lib/sber-server.ts and apps/web/components/sber-money-rail-panel.tsx are web presentation/proxy surfaces. They remain outside this foundation and cannot be used as proof of provider availability or transaction finality.
Sber Business ID/authentication is a distinct identity concern and must never be reused as settlement, billing, financing or callback authority.

Current official public documentation exists for Sber, Alfa-Bank and T-Bank nominal-account/payment platform scenarios. Public documentation proves discoverability/specification only; it does not prove this organization's contract, credentials, IntegrationBinding maturity, callback trust or settlement finality.

Alfa-Bank public payment status vocabulary and T-Bank HTTP success responses are provider-specific transport/business states. They must be mapped behind the provider-neutral port and must never become canonical Settlement state names by string reuse.
requiredInvariants: Bank/provider choice is an adapter concern. Core SettlementPlan/FinancialObligation semantics remain provider-neutral and no Sber-, Alfa- or T-Bank-only field enters canonical money authority.

Capabilities are explicit and versioned, including reserve/release safe-deal-like flow, direct payment/billing, financing/application, statements/status and callback/reconciliation support; unsupported capability fails closed.

Sber, Alfa-Bank and T-Bank mappings remain NOT_ACTIVATED/unknown for real traffic until the canonical Provider/IntegrationBinding authority has current server-held evidence and the concrete settlement operation is bound to that provider/binding.

Adapter request/response contracts use exact minor units, immutable operation/idempotency identifiers and the canonical settlement source versions; no Float money or browser-computed amount becomes authority.

An outbound accepted/queued request, HTTP 2xx or provider transport acknowledgement is not bank finality. Only validated provider evidence bound to exact operation/provider/key/payload fingerprint plus canonical reconciliation can advance final settlement authority.

The same router contract accepts Sber, Alfa-Bank and T-Bank reference/conformance mappings plus test doubles without changing Settlement core, proving provider substitution rather than one-provider lock-in.
Credential/key/revocation authority remains server-side. Browser, Deal participant or adapter cannot select arbitrary tenant/provider identity or callback key.
Callback replay, mismatched amount/currency/operation/provider, stale key and unknown event fail closed and cannot create duplicate ledger movements.
Example env values, UI provider registries, mock handlers, display panels, public developer docs and historical docs are non-authoritative and cannot satisfy live-provider or multi-bank acceptance.
Bank identity/authentication products or user sessions must not be accepted as bank-operation authorization, settlement finality, callback authenticity, billing approval or financing approval.
Financing readiness is a capability/application lifecycle only; adapter availability does not imply approved financing, credit limit or funds.
Billing readiness is separate from safe-deal/reserve-release readiness; one provider capability cannot be silently reused as another.
No live Sber, Alfa-Bank or T-Bank claim is emitted by fixtures, docs or UI until production receipts are evidenced on REG.RU and server-held maturity permits real traffic.
Registration, Role Eligibility, Federal Accounting lock #4321, packages/lockfiles and production topology remain unchanged.
acceptance: Contract tests prove the provider-neutral adapter/receipt vocabulary and capability matrix has no Sber-, Alfa- or T-Bank-only field in canonical core types.
Sber, Alfa-Bank and T-Bank reference/conformance adapters satisfy the same port/router contract, while at least two independent test doubles can be swapped without Settlement core changes.
Every provider mapping fails NOT_ACTIVATED or equivalent fail-closed state without production credentials/config/server-held LIVE_ACCEPTED evidence and never fabricates SUCCESS.
Exact amount/currency/idempotency/callback/provider/operation matching and duplicate/replay/mismatched receipt cases are tested fail closed.

Focused regressions prove BANK_MODE/BANK_PROVIDER example configuration, web provider metadata, mocks, public developer docs and bank identity sessions cannot satisfy bank authority or finality checks.
HTTP 2xx, accepted, queued, IN_PROGRESS/AWAIT_EXTERNAL or analogous provider-specific statuses are not treated as canonical finality without provider evidence and reconciliation.
Capability absence separately blocks safe-deal, billing, statements/status or financing actions rather than degrading to another bank function.
Existing settlement reconciliation/key rotation/hash-chain tests remain green and no new mutation authority bypasses them.
No secret, credential or paid dependency is committed; new mandatory recurring cost remains 0 RUB.
Exact-head CI/review and later REG.RU credentialed acceptance are required before terminal multi-bank credit.
remainingTerminalBoundary: Real Sber, Alfa-Bank and T-Bank contracts/credentials/endpoints and authentic provider receipts remain external dependencies unless separately obtained and accepted.
The canonical bank-settlement read/binding contract must link a concrete Deal/operation to Provider/IntegrationBinding maturity before PRODUCT can truthfully name its runtime bank authority.
W5-A SettlementPlan consumer wiring must exist before adapters can move real canonical obligations.
At least two real providers with accepted production evidence are required to prove terminal production multi-bank substitution; reference/test adapters are foundation evidence only.

sources.finding: Official Sber developer documentation describes Safe Deals over nominal accounts and test/industrial connection flows.
Official Alfa API documentation describes nominal accounts for platforms/marketplaces, including safe-deal and direct-payout scenarios.
Official Alfa API documentation exposes nominal-account payment status reads with explicit processing/failure/success states.
Official T-API documentation lists payments/statuses, statements, nominal accounts and credit products for direct/partner integrations.
Official T-Bank developer documentation exposes nominal-account methods for beneficiaries, billing, deals and deal stages.
